slot.brief: Which alkyl halide and alkoxide combination gives the best yield of a specified ether via Williamson synthesis (avoid 3° halides)?

stem: Which reagent combination gives the best yield of tert-butyl methyl ether by Williamson synthesis?

verdicts.working: Williamson ether synthesis proceeds by SN2, so use tert-butoxide with methyl iodide: attack at methyl forms tert-butyl methyl ether. Tertiary bromide in (B) or (C) favors elimination; (D) gives dimethyl ether.

working:
Williamson synthesis proceeds by $\mathrm{S_N2}$ attack of an alkoxide on an alkyl halide.\nA methyl halide is least hindered: $(\text{CH}_3)_3\text{CO}^- + \text{CH}_3\text{I} \longrightarrow (\text{CH}_3)_3\text{COCH}_3$.

Independent check: Williamson ether synthesis proceeds by SN2, so use tert-butoxide with methyl iodide: attack at methyl forms tert-butyl methyl ether. Tertiary bromide in (B) or (C) favors elimination; (D) gives dimethyl ether.
solution:
Williamson ether synthesis proceeds by an $\mathrm{S_N2}$ reaction, so the alkyl halide should be least hindered.
$$
(\mathrm{CH_3})_3\mathrm{CO^-} + \mathrm{CH_3I} \longrightarrow (\mathrm{CH_3})_3\mathrm{COCH_3}
$$
Methyl iodide gives substitution readily, yielding tert-butyl methyl ether.
